title: Covert spatial selection in primate basal ganglia
verification: Full primary article retrieved directly from PLOS via urllib; Methods and Figure 1 text read. Firecrawl extraction failed at the service layer; this is not an article-access limitation.
support_location: Materials and methods: Motion-direction CD task; Figure 1A; Results: Visual motion-change detection task
supports: A peripheral ring marks the relevant patch; target direction changes require a response whereas foil changes and catches do not.
Two patch means differ by 90°; 16° Gaussian angular SD; 10-frame/100-ms lifetime; 15°/s; aperture radius 3–3.75° and median 3.25°; mean eccentricity 12°.
Primary timing is 0.2-s cue, 0.5-s gap, event at 1.0–4.3 s after motion onset, and response window of 1 s. Event mixture is 57/29/14.
26°/28° are monkey-specific median threshold-adjusted changes, not the complete original stimulus distribution.
does_not_support: The 100×100 raster, 16-dot count, bilinear splats, exact birth law, randomly interleaved target side, and shortened final-report protocol are project adaptations.
Does not validate the four-Gabor ring task or plus/minus signed-orientation rule.
Does not establish any biological mechanism or learned model performance in this atlas.
verified_excerpts: The direction of motion in the cued and foil patch was varied day to day but always differed by 90 degrees.
The proportions of trials with a motion-direction change at the cued location or foil location or had no change were 57%, 29%, and 14%, respectively.

authors: Valerio Mante; David Sussillo; Krishna V. Shenoy; William T. Newsome
title: Context-dependent computation by recurrent dynamics in prefrontal cortex
type: primary empirical neuroscience with computational modeling
verification: Full author manuscript retrieved from PMC and independently from Europe PMC XML; task description and Figure 1 inspected.
support_location: Main text introducing context-dependent selection; Figure 1; Online Methods: Behavioral task
supports: Monkeys used a contextual cue to choose whether motion or color was relevant in a random-dot display.

does_not_support: Not a spatial plus/minus Gabor experiment or a replication of the suite signed rule.
No claim that its recurrent network is required for these tasks or that this atlas measures the same population dynamics.
verified_excerpts: The monkeys were instructed by a contextual cue to either discriminate the direction of motion or the color of a random-dot display, and to report their choices with a saccade to one of two visual targets

Two items were presented on the screen, one previously seen old item, and one new foil item.
